This is a normalized measure that enables comparison across teams and games. The underlying assumption is that formation data is consistently tagged and available. The computation of under-center EPA/play introduces a second-order metric that weights each snap by its expected points added (eEPA), allowing for nuanced performance analysis. These primitives form the basis of a dual system: one for static formation classification and another for dynamic value estimation. The failure mode occurs when formation tagging is inconsistent or absent, leading to undefined or misleading rates. The SumerPass pricing model acts as an access control layer, influencing data availability and thus the reliability of these metrics. The GSE uses this data to model situational behavior, while GSI applies Bayesian inference to estimate performance distributions.
